rules.claim: The detail notes action accepts GET and POST and applies PaperlessNotePermissions.
The addressed resource is loaded as Document with pk equal to the action's pk, including its owner.
The acting principal is request.user, assigned to currentUser.
PaperlessNotePermissions maps GET to documents.view_note and documents.view_document model permissions.
PaperlessNotePermissions maps POST to documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document model permissions.
Before method dispatch, a non-null currentUser must pass has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, view_document, addressed document), otherwise the action returns forbidden.
GET is denied with insufficient permissions when the shared view_document owner-aware check fails.
GET serializes and returns the addressed document's notes after the shared object check.
POST first traverses the same owner-aware view_document check used before method dispatch.
POST then requires a non-null currentUser to pass has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, change_document, addressed document), otherwise it returns forbidden.
POST is denied by the shared pre-dispatch check if owner-aware view_document authorization fails.
POST is denied with insufficient permissions to create notes if owner-aware change_document authorization fails.
POST creates a Note bound to the addressed document and current user, then returns the document's notes.

rules.claim: The document notes operation is exposed as a detail action supporting GET and POST.
The endpoint-level permission map requires documents.view_note and documents.view_document for GET.
The endpoint-level permission map requires documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document for POST.
The operation loads the addressed Document by pk and also loads its owner.
Before method dispatch, GET and POST require has_perms_owner_aware(request.user, view_document, addressed document), otherwise the operation returns forbidden.
POST additionally requires has_perms_owner_aware(request.user, change_document, addressed document), otherwise note creation is rejected.
The owner-aware helper returns true when the document has no owner, when the owner equals the request user, or when the object permission checker grants the requested permission.
After the GET checks, the handler serializes the addressed document's notes and returns them.
Failure of the handler's owner-aware view_document check returns HTTP forbidden before notes are returned.
After POST checks, the handler creates a Note attached to the addressed document and returns the serialized notes.
Failure of the initial owner-aware view_document check rejects POST before note creation.
Failure of the POST owner-aware change_document check rejects note creation.

rules.claim: The document detail notes action is exposed for GET and POST and declares PaperlessNotePermissions as its permission class.
The endpoint-level GET permission map requires documents.view_note and documents.view_document.
Before GET note serialization, the addressed Document is checked with has_perms_owner_aware(request.user, view_document, doc); failure returns forbidden.
If the GET object check does not reject, the handler serializes and returns the addressed document's notes.
If the GET view_document object check fails, the endpoint returns forbidden and does not reach the notes response.
The endpoint-level POST permission map requires documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document.
POST first applies the addressed Document view_document owner-aware check; failure returns forbidden before note creation.
After the initial view check, POST applies the addressed Document change_document owner-aware check; failure returns forbidden before Note.objects.create.
If the POST checks do not reject, the handler creates a Note attached to the addressed Document.
If the POST view_document check fails, the endpoint rejects before note creation.
If the POST change_document check fails, the endpoint rejects before Note.objects.create.

The owner-aware helper returns true when the Document has no owner or when its owner equals the request user, otherwise it requires checker.has_perm(perms, obj); ownership is therefore an implementation branch distinct from an object grant.
A GET may reach the notes response through the owner/no-owner branch of has_perms_owner_aware without source evidence of a view_document object grant.
A POST may reach Note.objects.create through the owner/no-owner branch of has_perms_owner_aware without source evidence of a change_document object grant.
